newsitem.title: USA: NYSE program trading averages 11.2 pct of volume.
newsitem.headline: NYSE program trading averages 11.2 pct of volume.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading amounted to 11.2 percent of its average daily volume of 460.8 million shares, or 51.4 million shares a day for the week of November 4-8.
For the prior week, program trading was 11.6 percent of its average daily volume of 443.8 million shares, or 51.3 million shares per day.
Of the average 51.4 million shares a day during the week, buy programs accounted for 7.7 percent and sell programs accounted for 3.5 percent.
In all markets, program trading averaged 67.9 million shares a day during November 4-8.

The NYSE's program trading report includes profiles of program trading whenever the Dow Jones Industrial Average moves 50 points or more in a single direction during any one-hour period. There were two such periods this week, both occuring Wednesday November 6.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, First Boston and Lehman Bros executed most of their program activity for their own accounts. First Options, Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers executed all or most of their program activity for customers, as agents or facilitator.
During November 4-8, 29.0 percent of program volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage, while another 21.0 percent involved derivative product-related strategies.
